decision: measured the laptop webcam before designing anything

decision: leading design is one WebGL2 shader core in TypeScript used by a web page, a browser extension and a desktop app

result: to be confirmed by prototypes and research

decision: recorded 9 clips of the same scene under forced camera states (as found, 30 fps auto, 50 Hz, dim, dark, very dark, high gain, two colour casts)
why: same scene in good and bad states lets us score output against the best state instead of guessing
result: 9 clips, about 136 frames each, camera restored

decision: checked which camera controls Chrome exposes for this webcam
why: the web design only works if the browser can run its own exposure control

decision: kept the name Sunroom and the plan to both drive the camera and repair the picture

result: gap confirmed; Zero-DCE and SCI licences rule them out for shipping

decision: scoring harness: exact camera frames, independent face boxes, same-scene reference, three naive baselines
why: every version must be judged before vs after on the same footage, not by eye alone
result: raw and baselines scored

decision: no neural network in version 1; classical GPU pipeline; history clamped by min/max; faces only lifted when below a healthy band
why: research found the well-known low-light models are non-commercial or unlicensed and too slow for integrated graphics
result: adopted

decision: v0: deflicker rows, motion-aware temporal denoise, guided-filter tone mapping anchored on the face
why: first full pass to see where it breaks
result: faces fixed on realistic clips; blue-cast clip turned to colour garbage; dark areas stayed noisy

decision: replaced SNR with noise in display units plus contrast-to-noise, and made colour error lightness-normalised
why: SNR rewarded the gamma baseline for flattening contrast, and raw colour distance punished correct brightening
result: fairer table

decision: v1: noise model per brightness band, spatial fill-in where history is thin, white balance capped with desaturation fallback, near-black colour drained
why: v0 pictures showed dark areas not accumulating and uncorrectable casts amplified
result: contrast-to-noise 52.8 vs raw 26.1 and gamma 27.9 on 6 realistic clips; dark noise 2.25 vs gamma 6.94; 10 to 18 ms per frame on Intel UHD

decision: did not register the virtual camera filter; stopped at the blocked step
why: the safety classifier refused the per-user registry write as persistence, and that is the owner's call to make
evidence: blocked PowerShell call in transcript; DLLs only downloaded to %LOCALAPPDATA%/sunroom/vcam
result: BLOCKED: per-user DirectShow registration is unproven until the owner allows the test

decision: desktop shell will be Electron, frames go out through koffi; browser extension uses MediaStreamTrackProcessor and Generator, never requestAnimationFrame
why: Tauri needs Rust and MSVC which this machine lacks; rAF freezes in background tabs
result: adopted

decision: live test on the real webcam from the as-found state: director pins the shutter and raises sensor gain
why: the web design only pays off if the app can undo the camera's frame-rate drop by itself
result: VERIFIED: 14.9 fps to 30 fps within 3 s, face luma about 106, 9 to 11 ms per frame, camera restored on stop

decision: added a gain ceiling with headroom check after seeing gain bounce 4 to 5 every second
why: raise and lower rules overlapped, so the loop cycled; clipped highlights cannot be recovered but a dark face can

decision: measured the denoiser alone: noise halves and banding drops about 80 percent with no detail loss, but stalls there
why: this camera's noise is correlated across frames, so averaging has a ceiling; added a spatial stage with a floor on assumed remaining noise
result: v3 crops visibly cleaner on the high-gain clip; temporal metric nearly unchanged, as expected for a spatial filter

decision: reverted to a wider plausible-skin range after colour errors rose in v3
